references.text: Describes the Lord as the great and awesome God, using similar expressions like 'el gadol' (great God) and 'nora' (awesome)
Moses exhorts the people not to fear, because the Lord will fight for them - the same theme of not being afraid of enemies
Joshua is commanded not to fear, because the Lord his God is with him - the same promise of God's presence and encouragement to be courageous
Joshua assures the people that the living God is in their midst and will drive out the nations - God's presence among them
Nehemiah describes God as the great and awesome God - uses the same Hebrew expression 'el gadol venora'
The Lord Most High is awesome, a great king over all the earth - the same theme of God's greatness and reverence
The Holy One of Israel is great in your midst - the same theme of the great God dwelling among his people
The Lord your God is in your midst, a mighty one who saves - a similar promise of God's powerful presence among his people
